analyzed_vuln.description: `MqttClient_Unsubscribe` unconditionally frees `unsubscribe->ack.props` after waiting for an UNSUBACK, but it never initializes/clears `unsubscribe->ack.props` at function entry and does not verify that a valid v5 UNSUBACK property list was actually decoded. As a result, `ack.props` can contain attacker-influenced stale/garbage pointer data, which is passed to `MqttClient_PropsFree` -> `MqttProps_Free`, causing traversal of an invalid linked list pointer and a wild read/SEGV at `head->type`/`head->next`. Crash occurs in `MqttProps_Free`, but root cause is unsafe state handling in `MqttClient_Unsubscribe` before calling free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires reaching `MqttClient_Unsubscribe` (fuzzer `unsubscribe()` path) with MQTT v5 property handling enabled, and causing `unsubscribe->ack.props` to be non-NULL but invalid (e.g., uninitialized/stale due to missing reset or malformed/partial UNSUBACK decode path). After `MqttClient_WaitType` returns, the code checks only `ack.props != NULL` and calls `MqttClient_PropsFree` on it, leading to invalid pointer dereference during property-list walk.
